statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. CME equity-index futures remain halted since the Friday settle, so no Nasdaq-100 price path exists in any hour of this horizon and Tail is held at a closed-venue floor.
recommendation: Tail holds a closed-venue floor of 4-5% across all 24 published hours, so the deterministic mapping stays EA_ON and green throughout. Stress drifts from 42% to 50%, entering the elevated band from 18:00 UTC on 5 September, reflecting hawkish September rate pricing after Friday's payroll beat, a Strait of Hormuz energy premium and a published trade-policy threat, all carried unpriced across the halt. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100 unquoted at 29,544.15 through the CME weekend halt, with the full 24-hour horizon ending about nine hours before the Sunday restart, so Tail holds a closed-venue floor while hawkish September rate pricing, a Hormuz energy premium and a trade-policy threat accumulate unpriced
body: The Nasdaq-100 closed the August payroll session on Friday 4 September at 29,544.15, up 61.85 points or 0.21% from a 29,482.30 previous close, having ranged between 29,440.15 and 29,655.22. Price retraced repeatedly in both directions during that session, which is the opposite of the persistent no-retracement structure the Tail score measures. Reuters reports August nonfarm payrolls up 162,000 against a consensus near 56,000 with the unemployment rate unchanged at 4.1%, and the priced probability of a quarter-point increase at the 15-16 September FOMC meeting rising to 58.4% from 49.4% the previous day. The Federal Reserve H.15 release carries the two-year Treasury yield at 4.34% and the ten-year at 4.77%. The VIX settled at 14.53, up 1.47% from 14.32 and still far below any level associated with disorderly repricing. Index internals on Friday were narrow rather than aligned: the S&P 500 closed 0.38% lower and the Dow 0.51% lower while semiconductors gained about 3.4%, and the megacap tape was split with three of eight names higher, Tesla down 5.92% and Apple down 2.51%. That is an internally mixed signature rather than the aligned cross-asset stack a genuine tail regime requires. Energy remains the principal unresolved input: WTI settled at $91.48 after a weekly advance near 10% and Brent at $92.68 after a 7.6% week, driven by renewed US-Iran strikes and continued impairment of Strait of Hormuz shipping, where only about four tankers transited on Thursday against a ten-day average near fifteen, with average US retail diesel at a record $5.85 per gallon. A separate trade-policy channel opened on Friday afternoon when the US President publicly threatened trade embargoes against countries with which the United States runs a deficit unless the Federal Reserve lowers rates; the statement is already published and entirely unpriced. CME equity-index futures have been halted since the 21:00 UTC Friday settle and are scheduled to reopen at 22:00 UTC on Sunday 6 September, roughly nine hours after the last hour published here. No forecast hour in this assessment can therefore contain an observable price path, and Tail is scored at a closed-venue floor throughout rather than from any directional view. Stress carries the accumulating weight of a hawkish September rate path, an energy-supply premium feeding the inflation outlook, an unresolved military exchange with an open weekend headline window, a new trade-policy threat, and a data-heavy week ahead containing August PPI on 10 September and August CPI on 11 September. The first genuine price-path evaluation of the new week belongs to a later assessment run after the Globex restart.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours cover the closing seven hours of the August payroll session and the first seventeen hours of the CME weekend halt. The 14:00 UTC hour on 4 September was already past the release peak at Tail 18% and Stress 58% under an event/whipsaw mode, and every slot in this window maps to EA_ON and green. Tail then decayed steadily through the US cash session as the index retraced its highs and recovered, with mode moving to mixed from 15:00 UTC as semiconductor leadership diverged from a softer broad tape, reaching Tail 12% and Stress 48% by 20:00 UTC. From the 21:00 UTC futures settlement onward every hour has been scored at the closed-venue floor of Tail 5%, with Stress easing to 38% and then drifting back to 41% by 13:00 UTC and mode normal. All 24 slots carry a published Claude assessment.
outlookSummary: The entire 24-hour horizon falls inside the CME weekend halt, so no observable Nasdaq-100 price path can form in any published hour and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON throughout. Tail is held at a 4-5% closed-venue floor, easing to 4% through the dormant middle of the weekend and returning to 5% as the horizon tracks back toward the venue timeline. Stress drifts from 42% to 50%, entering the elevated band from 18:00 UTC on 5 September, reflecting hawkish September rate pricing after Friday's payroll beat, an energy premium from continued Strait of Hormuz disruption, a published trade-policy threat tied to Fed rate demands, and an open two-sided weekend headline window. Confidence eases from 85% to 78% purely through the ageing of Friday-anchored evidence and stays inside the high band because the evidence set remains complete. The horizon ends at 13:00 UTC on 6 September, roughly nine hours before the scheduled 22:00 UTC Globex restart, so the reopening auction and any gap it produces belong to a later assessment run.
